extracted.intended_audience: writers of literary fiction; creative-writing students and instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and theoretical criteria for producing literary fiction that preserves a 'half-known' zone of mystery while remaining communicative; covers POV, accidental features ('spandrels'), politics and art, worldbuilding, voice, and moral demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Half-Known World
rubrics_metrics.description: "There must be a dimension to the fictional reality that escapes comprehension." Literary fiction must confront regions of human experience that aren't fully susceptible to rational understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance: a story that explains everything fails as art; one that leaves too much unknown fails as communication. Aim for the zone between full explanation and total obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and Paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: How writers approach the work — the methods, habits, and overarching models by which a writer organizes the act of fiction-writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider your working paradigm and process as part of craft: how you begin, revise, and the paradigms that shape what you notice and preserve in a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Spandrels
rubrics_metrics.description: The accidental architectural by-products that often turn out essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to accidental details or structural by-products ('spandrels') — what seems incidental can become the organizing principle of the piece. Be open to letting accidental discoveries reshape the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Omniscience (POV / Authorial Knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of point of view and how much the narrator/author knows and reveals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat choices about omniscience and POV as central craft decisions: decide who knows what, when, and why. POV choices control the half-knownness of the work and are not merely technical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban Legends, Pornography, and Literary Fiction (Genre vs. Literary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consideration of genre, the obscene, and markers of literary craft — how genre elements intersect with literary ambitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand how genre conventions or 'obscene' material can be used as craft tools; genre boundaries can be exploited or transcended, but such use should serve literary aims rather than merely shock or titillate.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Alternate Universe (Fictional Reality Construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction of a fictional reality — the rules, consistencies, and texture that make an invented world persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a consistent, convincing alternate universe: details should cohere to create verisimilitude while allowing for the half-known dimension; selective revelation of rules sustains mystery without breaking credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politics and Art in the Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: How engagement with political matters and the world can coexist with literary craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political engagement need not compromise literary quality; craft decisions should allow political concerns to be present without reducing the work to polemic. Balance engagement and artistic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Eye Point of View (POV / Voice Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of voice and POV through the example of private-eye narration — how a distinctive voice shapes what is known and unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a voice that shapes what the reader can access; voice-driven POVs provide a moral and epistemic filter that can heighten the half-knownness or clarity as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: You Must Change Your Life (Fiction as Moral Demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rilke-inspired idea: fiction as a call or demand that affects the moral life of writer and reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider fiction's ethical/moral dimension: stories may function as moral provocations or invitations to change. The writer's seriousness and moral stakes can power craft decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction must mystify, not merely explain
rubrics_metrics.description: A thematic quality implication: fiction's role is to mystify rather than to provide full explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-exposition and exhaustive explanation; preserve elements that resist tidy interpretation so the work registers as art rather than encyclopedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensibility ≠ Knowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters can be understood without being fully knowable — comprehension of motive/behavior is not the same as complete knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for characters whose actions and inner lives are intelligible enough to matter but resist complete decoding; allow ambiguity in interiority while providing sufficient cues for empathy and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spandrels matter
rubrics_metrics.description: What seems accidental often becomes essential to the story's architecture and meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to incidental elements in drafting and revision; what began as a minor detail may prove crucial to theme, structure, or climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politics + Art coexist
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with political subjects does not preclude literary craft; the two can coexist productively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate political material through craft choices (voice, POV, structure) rather than allowing politics to flatten complexity or dominate aesthetic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV is a moral choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting point of view is not merely technical but a moral decision shaping what the reader is asked to know or withhold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make POV choices deliberately, aware of ethical implications: who gets to tell the story, whose consciousness is centered, and what the consequences are for reader judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reader's incomprehension is part of the experience
rubrics_metrics.description: A reader's inability to fully comprehend is a feature, not a flaw; incomprehension contributes to the work's effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the narrative so that some withholding and difficulty are intentional; trust the reader to live with unresolved aspects rather than over-explaining to avoid discomfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the story preserve real mystery?
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: evaluate whether the story intentionally preserves areas of genuine mystery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge drafts by whether they leave room for meaningful unknowns that deepen rather than frustrate the reader; excise impulses to tidy every loose end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are characters knowable without being fully known?
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: determine if characters are presented so readers can understand them without full ontological disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess characterization for intelligibility plus indeterminacy — characters should invite empathy and curiosity without yielding exhaustive biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the reader emerge with new questions?
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: a strong story prompts readers to leave the text with further questions rather than only answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate endings and revelations for their ability to generate productive curiosity and reflection rather than merely resolving plot points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a 'spandrel' that turned out to organize the whole?
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: look for an accidental detail or element that becomes the organizing principle of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During revision, identify and amplify emergent spandrels that provide coherence; resist the urge to force a different organizing center that undermines organic discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the ending stop short of explanation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality test: the ending should refrain from over-explaining and allow some closure to remain open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the final pages for restraint: endings that stop just short of full explanation often feel truer and more powerful than neatly tied-up conclusions.
